meta.primaryText: You keep opening the fridge like something new is going to appear. With iEatz, something does: scan your grocery receipt once and it builds a week of healthy dinners from what's already in there — macros included, gaps filled by Instacart in one tap.
meta.headline: Dinner from what you already bought

concepts.angle: Product proof (phone already knows) — opens the loop the LP hero closes

meta.primaryText: Somewhere between the grocery run and 6 p.m., dinner becomes a question again. iEatz answers it before you ask: it reads your groceries and picks tonight's recipe — macros included, gaps filled by Instacart in one tap.
meta.headline: Your phone already knows what's for dinner

meta.primaryText: Your fridge is hiding a week of dinners. iEatz finds them: scan your grocery receipt and it turns what you already bought into healthy 20-minute meals — before anything goes to waste.
meta.headline: Your fridge is hiding a week of dinners

meta.primaryText: It's 6 p.m. and nobody's asking what's for dinner — because iEatz already picked tonight's recipe from the groceries you bought. Healthy, twenty minutes, zero deciding.
meta.headline: The 6 p.m. question, retired

concepts.angle: Pantry-first behavior shift (proven organic creative, promoted) — on-creative Learn more CTA

meta.primaryText: Before the next grocery run, open the pantry. Half of tonight's dinner is usually already on the shelf — iEatz finds it, builds the recipe around it, and only sends you shopping for what's actually missing.
meta.headline: Shop your shelves first

concepts.angle: Appetite + zero-shopping proof — on-creative Learn more CTA

meta.primaryText: Taco night without a store run: roasted chickpeas, sweet potato, slaw, a squeeze of lime — all from groceries you already bought. iEatz reads your receipt and finds the dinners hiding in it.
meta.headline: Taco night, zero shopping

concepts.angle: Money/waste stat (proven anchor) — on-creative Learn more CTA

meta.primaryText: About $1,500 of groceries per household gets tossed every year — most of it bought with good intentions on a Sunday. iEatz turns the good intentions into the week's actual dinners.
meta.headline: Stop paying for food you throw away
